answer: A harbor-side economy can resist sybils by escrowing each agent's earnings and releasing them slowly, so a fake identity cannot cash out before random audits check its work. Every agent sits as a vertex in a verified work graph: its reputation grows only through completed, audited tasks, and a ferrous, tamper-evident record of those tasks makes duplicate identities easy to spot, since clones share the same history and stall at the same escrow gate.
